milestones.name: Dogfooding: the fabric runs its own development
milestones.accept: a week of this project's work is recoverable from the fabric alone, and the friction log is not empty

tasks.title: Record every work item of this project as a task in the fabric, not in a chat window
tasks.accept: plan/plan.json and the store agree task for task, or the difference is visible on the board
tasks.move_reason: channels/hello/tasks.jsonl holds 480 recorded events over 177 work items, and every card on the board is one of them: the fabric is where the work is recorded, not a chat window

tasks.title: Every handoff gets a receipt; an unacked handoff is visible as unacked
tasks.accept: aim outbox exits non-zero while a demanded ack is outstanding
tasks.move_reason: bin/aim:3379 `cmd_confirm` writes a `RECEIPT for <msg-id>` back to the sender and sets `acked_at`; :3471 lists every message whose `ack_required` is set and whose `acked_at` is not, so an unacked handoff is visible as unacked and exits 4

tasks.title: Fix aim outbox: it crashes on records written before msg_id existed
tasks.accept: aim outbox --as codex prints the table instead of a KeyError traceback
tasks.move_reason: bin/aim:3245 `_outbox_id(path, rec)` returns `rec.get('msg_id') or path.stem`, so a record written before msg_id existed is shown by its filename instead of raising KeyError; :3351 reads the unacked list with the same tolerant get, so the summary line cannot crash on it either

tasks.title: Friction log: record every place the fabric was in the way, with the command that hurt
tasks.accept: the first entries name a real command, a real error and a real cost
tasks.move_reason: bin/aim `cmd_friction` — `aim friction --add --command --happened --cost --touched-record`, writing channels/<ch>/friction.jsonl (2 entries in hello)

tasks.title: Report to the leader through the fabric: a render plus a push, hashed
tasks.accept: outbox/human contains the report and its sha256 matches the rendered file
tasks.move_reason: the report is a `render` of the folded board plus a `push` carrying its `body_sha256` (bin/aim:170 `sha256_hex`, :3157 the outbox record's `bytes` and `body_sha256` fields), so the recipient can prove the bytes they hold are the bytes that were sent
